text: An old potter had one tea bowl he loved above all others.
One rainy morning, his apprentice carried it across the garden,
slipped on a wet stone, and the bowl shattered.
"Forgive me, master! I will throw it away and make you a new one."
But the old potter knelt and gathered every piece.
Day after day, he joined them with lacquer and with gold.
"Why mend it?" the boy asked. "It will never be the same."
"No," said the potter. "It will be more beautiful."
And from then on, it was the bowl he poured for his dearest guests.
Your cracks are not your end. Mend them in gold.
